description: Representing what a system knows and drawing conclusions from it: propositional and first-order logic, inference and resolution, rule-based and expert systems, ontologies and semantic networks, reasoning under uncertainty with Bayesian networks, and automated planning. Taught through browser-based reasoners, a Prolog-style interpreter and a Bayesian-network tool, so every representation is encoded and every inference is run and checked.
modelledOn: Brachman and Levesque, Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
Russell and Norvig, Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
Poole and Mackworth, Artificial Intelligence: Foundations of Computational Agents
outcomes: Represent knowledge in propositional and first-order logic with correct syntax and semantics.
Perform inference by resolution, unification and forward and backward chaining.
Build rule-based and expert systems and explain their conclusions.
Model a domain with ontologies and semantic networks and reason over them.
Represent and reason about uncertain knowledge with Bayesian networks.
Formulate and solve planning problems and connect them to knowledge representation.

units.title: Knowledge, representation and reasoning
topics: What it means for a system to know something; the knowledge level versus the symbol level
Declarative versus procedural knowledge; the representation hypothesis
Entailment, soundness and completeness as the standards an inference method must meet
A survey of representations: logic, rules, frames, networks and probabilistic models
Applications: a crop-advisory assistant and a clinic triage aid for a rural health post

units.title: Propositional logic
topics: Syntax and semantics; truth tables, models and logical equivalence
Validity, satisfiability and entailment; the deduction theorem
Normal forms: conjunctive and disjunctive; converting to clauses
Model checking and the DPLL procedure for satisfiability
Encoding a scheduling or configuration constraint as a propositional formula

units.title: First-order logic
topics: Objects, relations and functions; constants, predicates, quantifiers and variables
Syntax and semantics of first-order logic; interpretations and models
Knowledge engineering: translating statements about a domain into first-order sentences
Expressing a family, organisation or geography ontology of Ghanaian regions and districts
The expressiveness and the decidability cost of first-order logic

units.title: Inference and resolution
topics: Inference rules; forward and backward chaining with Horn clauses
Unification and the most general unifier
Resolution refutation: converting to clausal form and proving by contradiction
Soundness, completeness and the search involved in finding a proof
A Prolog-style interpreter: facts, rules, queries and backtracking
Negation as failure and the closed-world assumption

units.title: Rules and expert systems
topics: Production systems: working memory, rule base and the inference engine
The match-resolve-act cycle and the Rete matching idea; conflict resolution
Forward- versus backward-chaining expert systems and when each fits
Explanation facilities and maintaining a rule base
Building a small diagnostic expert system for a common problem

units.title: Ontologies and semantic networks
topics: Semantic networks and frames; inheritance, defaults and exceptions
Ontologies: classes, individuals, properties and the subsumption hierarchy
Description logics as the formal basis; the open-world assumption
The semantic web stack: RDF triples, RDFS and OWL; querying a knowledge graph
Reasoning tasks: classification, consistency checking and instance retrieval
Modelling a local agriculture or health domain as an ontology

units.title: Reasoning under uncertainty
topics: Why strict logic is brittle for real knowledge; degrees of belief
Probability as a representation of uncertainty; the axioms and conditional probability
Bayes' rule and the naive Bayes assumption
Alternatives in brief: certainty factors, fuzzy logic and non-monotonic reasoning

units.title: Bayesian networks
topics: Representing a joint distribution compactly; conditional independence and the graph
Constructing a network and its conditional probability tables for a domain
Exact inference by enumeration and variable elimination
Approximate inference by sampling when exact inference is too costly
A diagnosis network for malaria-like symptoms at a clinic as a worked example

units.title: Planning
topics: Representing actions with preconditions and effects; the STRIPS and PDDL languages
State-space planning: forward and backward search and useful heuristics
Partial-order planning and planning graphs in brief
Planning as logical inference and as satisfiability; the link back to representation
Capstone: encode a logistics domain and have a planner produce and explain a plan

schedule.title: What knowledge representation is
schedule.exercise: Pick five facts a clinic nurse uses for triage and write them as rules, as a table and as a sentence in logic, noting what each form hides.

tasks.title: Write the same crop-advice knowledge once as if-then Python code and once as a data table of rules, and compare how each is changed
Test an inference function against a knowledge base of 10 facts, labelling each answer as sound, unsound or incomplete
Represent a rural health post triage problem in rules, frames and a probabilistic table, then compare the three on five test patients

schedule.title: Propositional logic
schedule.exercise: Use the deduction theorem to show that a set of premises entails a conclusion, and convert a formula to clauses by hand.

tasks.title: Enumerate all models of a 4-symbol formula with a truth-table checker and list which assignments make it true
Decide validity, satisfiability and entailment for six formula pairs using model enumeration and report the counts of models found
Write a converter that turns formulas into CNF clauses by eliminating implications and distributing, and test it on 8 formulas

schedule.title: SAT solving and encoding
schedule.exercise: Run DPLL by hand on a 6-clause formula, showing unit propagation and each branching decision.

tasks.title: Step through DPLL on a 5-variable formula, recording each unit propagation and decision, and report the satisfying assignment found
Encode a 3-colouring problem for a 6-node map as clauses and solve it with a small SAT routine, verifying the colouring
Encode a weekly timetable for 4 classes and 3 rooms with clash constraints as CNF, solve it and count how many clauses result

schedule.title: First-order logic
schedule.exercise: Translate eight English sentences about students and courses into first-order logic and say which have more than one reading.

tasks.title: Define a small family domain with constants and predicates in code and evaluate five quantified sentences against it
Check whether a given interpretation is a model of three first-order sentences and find one interpretation that falsifies the fourth
Translate 10 statements about a university registration system into first-order sentences and test them on a database of facts for errors

schedule.title: Ontologies in logic and its limits
schedule.exercise: Write down the sentences defining parent, sibling and cousin and a few facts about regions and districts, then list one question first-order logic cannot answer by computation.

tasks.title: Encode 12 facts about Ghana's regions and districts and write a rule that derives all districts in a given region
Define ancestor, cousin and in-law relations over a 15-person family tree and query them, checking five answers by hand
Show with a non-terminating rule set why inference over first-order logic can loop forever, then add a depth bound that restores termination

schedule.title: Chaining, unification and resolution
schedule.exercise: Unify four pairs of terms by hand, then prove a query by resolution refutation on a small knowledge base.

tasks.title: Run forward chaining on a Horn clause base of 8 rules, listing facts as they are derived, and stop when the goal is derived
Implement unification with an occurs check and test it on 10 term pairs including failing and cyclic cases
Prove a query by resolution refutation on a clause set, recording each resolvent, and compare the proof length with backward chaining

schedule.title: Proof search and a Prolog-style engine
schedule.exercise: Explain why the closed-world assumption makes 'not flooded' true for any region absent from a database and when that is dangerous.

tasks.title: Run five queries against a facts-and-rules program and trace which clause matches and where backtracking happens in each
Write a small backtracking interpreter for facts, rules and queries and check it on a family-relations knowledge base
Add negation as failure to your interpreter, then show a query where it gives a misleading answer under incomplete data

schedule.title: Production rules and expert systems
schedule.exercise: Compare forward and backward chaining for a diagnosis task and write the explanation facility's output for one conclusion.

tasks.title: Step through a production system cycle on 6 rules and 5 working-memory facts, recording matches and the rule fired each cycle
Implement conflict resolution by specificity and recency, and show how the order of fired rules changes on the same facts
Build a small expert system for diagnosing maize leaf problems with 15 rules and a why-explanation, tested on 10 cases

schedule.title: Frames, semantic nets and description logics
schedule.exercise: Draw a class hierarchy for farm animals with defaults and exceptions, and say what the open-world assumption means for an unstated fact.

tasks.title: Build a frame hierarchy of crops with slot inheritance and a default, then query three inherited values and one exception
Classify 10 individuals into a subsumption hierarchy by stepping through membership checks and draw the resulting graph
Express five concept definitions with existential and universal restrictions and compute subsumption among them by checking all instances

schedule.title: The semantic web and ontology modelling
schedule.exercise: Model five classes and four properties for malaria clinic data and list the three reasoning tasks your ontology should support.

tasks.title: Write 15 RDF triples about districts and crops and answer three pattern queries by matching the triples in code
Run RDFS style inference of types and subclasses over a small graph, and report the new triples that appear
Model a local agriculture domain with at least 8 classes, check consistency with disjoint classes and list instances found by retrieval

schedule.title: Reasoning under uncertainty
schedule.exercise: Apply Bayes' rule by hand to a malaria test with stated sensitivity, specificity and prevalence, and interpret the posterior.

tasks.title: Compute the probability of disease given a positive test for three prevalence levels and plot how the posterior changes
Train a naive Bayes classifier on 200 symptom records, report test accuracy and examine one prediction by its likelihood terms
Compare certainty factors, fuzzy membership and probability on the same five uncertain triage cases and discuss where they disagree

schedule.title: Bayesian networks
schedule.exercise: Draw a 5-node network for fever, malaria, typhoid, test result and travel, and fill in plausible conditional probability tables.

tasks.title: Build a three-node network and read its conditional probability tables to compute one joint probability by the chain rule
Compute a posterior in a 5-node network by enumeration and variable elimination and compare the number of multiplications used
Estimate a posterior in the malaria diagnosis network with rejection sampling and likelihood weighting, and compare error against exact inference

schedule.title: Planning and capstone
schedule.exercise: Describe the actions, preconditions and effects for a delivery of vaccines to three clinics, and explain how a planner would explain its plan.

tasks.title: Write STRIPS actions for moving a truck and loading a crate, then apply them to a start state to reach a goal by hand
Run forward state-space search on a 3-location logistics problem, comparing nodes expanded with and without a simple heuristic
Encode a logistics domain in PDDL-style actions, have a planner produce a plan and print the reason each action is in it
